claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Standard, unoptimized HVAF-i7 spraying of the 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable coating quality.
Standard, unoptimized HVAF-i7 spraying produces inadequate coating thickness.
Changing HVAF-i7 fuel/oxygen flows and spray distance can increase FeCoNiCrAl particle velocity.
A spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm is an appropriate optimization range for increasing particle velocity with the HVAF-i7 torch.
Increasing in-flight particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves particle flattening upon impact.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves bonding of deposited particles to the substrate.
Improved particle flattening and impact bonding enhance deposit build-up.
Faster particles produce more effective splat formation and bonding.
More effective splat formation and bonding increase deposition efficiency.
The increased deposition efficiency overcomes the HVAF-i7 coating-thickness limitation.
Increasing particle velocity under the proposed conditions maintains low as-sprayed oxidation.
The optimized HVAF-i7 process will produce thickness comparable to that obtained with the HVAF-M3 torch.
The optimized coating will retain acceptable adhesion.
The optimized coating will retain acceptable oxidation control.
The intervention is expected to remain effective for deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm and under high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.

contradictions.description: The proposed 300–350 mm spray distance appears geometrically incompatible with coating the wall of an internal diameter as small as 120 mm unless a special axial, angled, or remote-nozzle geometry is specified. The hypothesis and experiment do not explain how both constraints can be met.
